notice: Where machine learning may assist the Evidence Atlas and where it must not decide. M0 trains no model and activates no model.
principle: Rules first. ML may propose normalized metadata, resolve entities, classify and triage, detect possible duplicates, flag anomalies, assign confidence and route records to NEEDS_REVIEW. An ML-only value never satisfies a hard eligibility criterion, and ML never autonomously determines truth, validation, release inclusion, rankings or scores.

normalization_methods.description: Value copied from a source controlled vocabulary with an exact registry mapping.
Exact alias match in a versioned Atlas vocabulary.
Value proposed by an evaluated ML model with a confidence score.
No method produced a value; the field is UNKNOWN.

allowed_tasks.output: proposed instrument_family_id / instrument_model_id from free text
proposed links between sample aliases, studies and publications
proposed assay / evidence-domain class for a study
proposed duplicate clusters beyond exact-accession rules
priority ordering of catalog records for human/rule review
flags for implausible metadata (e.g. read length inconsistent with technology)
route a record to NEEDS_REVIEW with the proposal and its confidence

prohibited_decisions.reason: Hard-gate fields require authoritative metadata, deterministic normalization of it, or curator confirmation.
Truth comes from versioned truth resources and frozen protocols.
Benchmark outcomes come from frozen comparators, never from ML.
Benchmark context is conditional; no rankings are generated.
No trust or reliability score is generated without a separately validated method.
The Atlas is not a caller leaderboard.
Release membership requires rule/curation gates and a release manifest.
Validation gates are deterministic protocol checks.

rule_conflict_behaviour: If an ML proposal disagrees with a rule-derived or source-controlled value, the non-ML value stands and the record is flagged NEEDS_REVIEW; ML never overrides a rule.
deployment_requirements: All thresholds.activation_requirements satisfied and recorded in thresholds.activation_record (report paths and SHA-256).
Comparison against the rules-only baseline on the same frozen evaluation set.
Model, training-data snapshot, code commit and evaluation report versioned and checksummed.
Activation is a policy-version change reviewed by a human; it never happens implicitly.
Every ML-produced value stores model_id, model_version, confidence and input hash.

thresholds.statement: PROVISIONAL / INACTIVE / NOT VALIDATED / SUBJECT TO M2 CALIBRATION. These numbers are configuration placeholders, not scientific thresholds. No model exists in M0, so they have no evidential meaning.
thresholds.applies_to: Non-hard-gate catalog fields only, and only once active. Thresholds never let an ML value satisfy a hard eligibility gate.
thresholds.behaviour_while_inactive: Every ML proposal is routed to human review (REVIEW); no ML value is written as a normalized field automatically.

behaviour_when_active.confidence >= accept_threshold: ACCEPT_NON_GATE: may populate a non-hard-gate catalog field as ML_PROPOSED
behaviour_when_active.review_threshold <= confidence < accept_: REVIEW: proposal shown to a curator; field stays UNKNOWN

activation_requirements: frozen, checksummed evaluation set created before training
calibration analysis (reliability curve, expected calibration error)
abstention analysis (coverage and abstention rate at each candidate threshold)
error analysis of false accepts and false abstentions

model_registry.statement: No ML model is activated by M0.
